english.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice for asserting that something is true or strongly emphasizing an adjective or verb.

exampleSentences.english: I really forgot what you said.
exampleSentences.traditional: 我真係唔記得咗你講乜。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2 nei5 gong2 mat1

english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something is really or genuinely so.

exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 zan1 hai6 hou2 jau5 sam1 wo3

english.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial intensifier or disbelief marker.

exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 zan1 hai6 jiu3 ji4 gaa1 zau2

english.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for saying that something is really or genuinely the case.

exampleSentences.english: The egg tarts at this shop are truly delicious.
exampleSentences.traditional: 呢間舖嘅蛋撻真係好食。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 pou3 ge3 daan6 taat1 zan1 hai6 hou2 sik6

english.note: Use this when indeed means “truly,” and for emphatic “indeed,” especially before an adjective or verb.

exampleSentences.jyutping: nei5 zan1 hai6 hou2 lek1 wo3

english.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial intensifier for emphatic evaluations such as “absolutely brilliant.”

exampleSentences.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 zan1 hai6 hou2 zeng3

english.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice when “literally” is loose, informal emphasis or filler.

exampleSentences.english: I’m literally so tired I want to sleep on the floor.
exampleSentences.traditional: 我真係攰到想瞓喺地下。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 gui6 dou3 soeng2 fan3 hai2 dei6 haa6

english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that something is genuinely or truly the case.

exampleSentences.english: The milk tea at this cha chaan teng is genuinely good.
exampleSentences.traditional: 呢間茶記啲奶茶真係好飲。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ne1 gaan1 caa4 gei3 di1 naai5 caa4 zan1 hai6 hou2 jam2

english.note: Use 真係 when “all right” emphatically confirms that something really happened or is certainly true.

exampleSentences.english: Ming really did come first in the exam, all right.
exampleSentences.jyutping: aa3 ming4 zan1 hai6 haau2 dou3 dai6 jat1 ming4

english.note: Use this for emphatic or incredulous force when the English expletive does not need to sound vulgar.

exampleSentences.jyutping: zan1 hai6 gam3 dou1 dak1 gaa3

english.note: Use this when “actually” means “really” and adds emphasis rather than simply correcting the listener.

exampleSentences.jyutping: zan1 hai6 gam1 jat6 jit6 dou3 deng2 m4 seon6

english.note: For the actually or really sense, 真係 is the all-purpose spoken choice.

exampleSentences.english: This shop really is a good buy, right?
exampleSentences.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 pou3 zan1 hai6 dai2 maai5 gaa3 wo3

english.note: Use this when “properly” intensifies an adjective or reaction, as in being really tired.

exampleSentences.english: I am properly exhausted today and do not want to move.
exampleSentences.traditional: 我今日真係攰到唔想郁。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 gui6 dou3 m4 soeng2 juk1

english.note: Use 真係 before an adjective or evaluation when altogether means really or clearly, rather than completely.

exampleSentences.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 zan1 hai6 hou2 tai2

english.note: Use this when the emphatic sense is “indeed” or “really,” rather than a rhetorical tag such as “係咪先.”

exampleSentences.jyutping: gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 dung3 wo3

english.note: Use this when emphatically means ‘truly’ or ‘indeed’, especially in an informal assertion.

exampleSentences.english: The pineapple buns at this cha chaan teng are emphatically delicious.
exampleSentences.traditional: 呢間茶餐廳嘅菠蘿包真係好食。
exampleSentences.jyutping: ne1 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1 ge3 bo1 lo4 baau1 zan1 hai6 hou2 sik6

english.note: Use this as an emphatic intensifier in an exclamation where English uses “ever” for extra emphasis.

exampleSentences.jyutping: bin1 go3 zan1 hai6 wui5 gam2 joeng2 zou6 gaa3
